studies.summary:

studies.title: OCTANE: Adjuvant Liposomal Doxorubicin and Carboplatin for Early-stage Triple-negative Breast Cancer
studies.summary:
This clinical trial aims to evaluate the efficacy, safety, and exploratory measures of liposomal doxorubicin and carboplatin combination therapy in the adjuvant setting for early stage triple negative breast cancer (TNBC) patients.

The primary objective is to determine the effectiveness of liposomal doxorubicin and carboplatin in reducing the risk of recurrence for early stage TNBC patients.

The secondary objectives involve characterizing the safety and toxicity profile of the combination therapy. Adverse events rates will be assessed using the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events

studies.title: Investigating the Efficacy of Brain Octane® Oil on Cognition, Coordination, Reaction Time and Measurements of Physical Performance in Recreationally Active Adults
studies.summary:
This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel study investigating the efficacy of Brain Octane® Oil on cognition, coordination, reaction time and measurements of physical performance in recreationally active adults. Thirty eligible participants will consume the investigational product or placebo for 27 days. 15 participants will consume the investigational product and 15 participants will receive the placebo product to consume.

consumer_summary.what_it_is: Octane is a straight-chain alkane made of eight carbon atoms, best known to most of us as a highly volatile, energy-dense component of gasoline. While it is famous for fueling combustion engines, this simple hydrocarbon also appears in trace amounts in the natural world as a xenobiotic compound. In daily life, you are most likely to encounter its sharp, chemical scent at the fuel pump or in industrial solvents.
consumer_summary.found_in: Despite its industrial reputation, trace amounts of octane have been identified in familiar plants like avocados, olives, and St. John's wort. It is also found in aromatic botanicals such as witch hazel, vetiver, and catmint.
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: Researchers are primarily drawn to octane for its chemical properties as a solvent and its role in catalysis and molecular modeling. In the realm of biology and health, interest is highly preliminary, with scientists exploring whether specific octane derivatives or bicyclic octane compounds might hold biological activity. The current body of health-related research is entirely in the earliest stages of discovery (Oxford level 5), focusing on chemical synthesis and cellular interactions rather than formal clinical trials on the pure alkane.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Researchers are exploring whether specific octane derivatives, such as octane aether, might offer a new pathway for managing chronic pain.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized, placebo-controlled clinical trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of octane aether for non-specific chronic low back pain, such as the planned trial NCT07614568.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Scientists are investigating whether certain bicyclic octane compounds or derivatives could interact with cellular pathways involved in abnormal cell growth.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: An in vitro screening study applying isolated octane derivatives to human cell lines to measure effects on cell proliferation and apoptosis over 48 hours.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Early literature hints at the possibility that specific octane-based molecular structures might help protect neural tissues from stress.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: An animal study in a rodent model of neurodegeneration, administering a standardized octane derivative to assess changes in cognitive function and neuronal survival over a three-month period.

consumer_summary.cautions: Octane is a volatile hydrocarbon and industrial solvent; occupational exposure or inhalation carries acute toxic effects, and it is not consumed as a dietary supplement.
consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: The biological and health evidence for octane is currently unclassified or in the earliest stages of discovery (Oxford level 5), with most literature focusing on its chemical properties rather than physiological effects.
